title: kv-cache: smarter eviction + defragmentation, paging & spillover improvements
author: Maya Singh
description:
Context and motivation:
We have ongoing production noise from KV cache fragmentation and memory churn that increases the frequency of host paging and NVMe spillover under tail workloads. This PR introduces a coordinated set of changes to reduce fragmentation, make eviction decisions size-aware, and provide safer paging/spillover fallbacks when GPU memory pressure is high. The goal is to reduce OOMs and tail latency regressions while preserving throughput for steady-state traffic.

What this changes (summary):
- Add multi-bucket eviction policy (size-aware + recency buckets) to prioritize evicting many small or stale entries before large hot spans.
- Background defragmentation worker that coalesces free segments during low-load windows. Defrag is rate-limited and bounded by a per-GPU memory budget.
- Paging/spillover improvements: when eviction cannot free enough contiguous memory, we now page cold KV pages to host pinned buffers and spill very large cold spans to NVMe with async background uploads.
- Continuous-batching integration: KV lookup path now signals the scheduler with a small hint when an access will trigger a defragmentation or spill to avoid batching hot requests with cold ones (reduces latency SLO violations).
- Telemetry: new metrics and traces for eviction decisions, defrag runs, pages moved to host, and NVMe spill counts. Added dashboards and alert tuning suggestions.

Checklist:
- [x] Multi-bucket eviction implementation (algorithm + tests)
- [x] Background defrag worker + config knobs (intervals, budget)
- [x] Paging & NVMe spill path with fallbacks and throttles
- [x] Scheduler hint integration + small scheduler change to respect hints
- [x] Unit and integration tests for eviction and paging paths
- [x] Local perf benchmarks and canary config for rollout
- [x] Docs: runtime/kv_cache.md updated with config and operational notes

Performance / safety notes:
- On our internal batch of synthetic load + production-like trace, we see 8-12% higher aggregate throughput under mixed seq-len workloads and ~75% reduction in OOM/recovery incidents for the canary cluster.
- Tail latency p95 impact is neutral in steady-state; during a deliberate memory pressure test the new scheduler hints reduced 99th percentile latency spikes by ~30% compared to master.
- Default defrag budget is conservative (2% of GPU mem) and disabled for Dedicated nodes unless explicitly enabled via config.

Rollout plan:
- Canary on canary-2 for 48h with metrics monitored (eviction_rate, defrag_runs, nvme_spills, host_pages).
- If canary stable, gradual rollout to low-traffic regions over 7 days with automatic rollback if OOM rate increases or NVMe spill rate > threshold.

Related: Linear ENG-4210 (KV cache fragmentation), ENG-4388 (spillover design docs). See design note: https://linear.app/redwood/issue/ENG-4210/kv-cache-fragmentation-defrag-and-spillover

review_comments: Evan Brooks (review): Can you clarify how the size-aware buckets determine priority? The algorithm looks reasonable but we need to ensure it doesn't thrash when workload mixes lots of medium-sized keys.

Maya Singh (reply): The policy uses three buckets (small/medium/large) with tunable size thresholds. Eviction prefers small buckets first and applies LFU weighting inside each bucket. I added a detailed comment and unit tests that exercise mixed workloads.
Luis Ortega (review): Defrag worker looks good but please add a safety check so defrag doesn't run while GPU is >80% busy (we've observed defrag contention previously).
Maya Singh (reply): Added a busy-check and a config knob defrag.max_gpu_util (default 0.8). Also added an integration test that simulates high util and verifies defrag is skipped.

Rina Nakamura (review): CI failed linting on first run (formatting). After fixes the integration CI run flaked once on network in the NVMe test; I re-ran and it passed. Approving pending the small nits.
Evan Brooks (approval): Approving. Please make sure ops team has the dashboard links and the canary manifest documented before merge.
release_notes: Improved KV cache memory management: size-aware eviction buckets, background defragmentation, safer host paging and NVMe spillover, scheduler hint integration for reduced tail latency. Default behavior conservative; enable additional tuning for Dedicated. See ops/docs/runtime/kv_cache.md for configuration and rollout notes.
notes_ops: Dashboards: runtime/kv_cache/eviction, runtime/kv_cache/defrag, runtime/kv_cache/spillover. Canary manifest added at ops/canary/manifests/kv-cache-canary.yaml. Default defrag budget is 2% GPU mem and disabled for Dedicated clusters by default.
